messages:
maria: FYI I ran the stage-split concurrency limiter experiment on prod-sim, results & notes below
aj: nice, quick summary?
maria: tl;dr: separating 'init/prefill' and 'gen/decode' into distinct batching lanes + a soft concurrency limiter reduced tail p99 by ~18% for short prompts, but we exposed KV thrash when cold-warm transitions hit the same worker. logs + config below.
tim: can you paste the numbers and the config we used?
maria: microbench:
- baseline (shared batcher): p50 11ms, p95 120ms, p99 360ms
- staged lanes + limiter: p50 10ms, p95 85ms, p99 295ms
- cost: +3% GPU util, -7% token efficiency due to slightly smaller average decode batches
lee: interesting. where did KV cache pressure show up?
maria: saw repeated KV eviction spikes in perf-bot dump when a prefill-heavy spike landed on the same device as a long-running decode stream. eviction rate ~2.4x vs baseline during the 60s window.
perf-bot: PROFILE SNAPSHOT (3319001500): kv_evictions: 240 -> 570 (60s window), kernel_switches: +12%, avg_kv_lookup_latency: 3.6ms -> 5.1ms
olga: did we change kernel selection or quant paths? those can amplify cache churn if execution layout changes.
maria: no quant changes. kernel affinity tweak: we forced decodes -> kernel-family-B for streaming memory layout. that shifted working set.
aj: can you share the scheduler snippet? want to see token budgets + queue policy.
maria: scheduler YAML we ran:
```yaml
stage_lanes:
  prefill:
    max_concurrency: 80
    token_budget_target: 51200 # bytes per second-ish target scaler
    batch_deadline_ms: 8
  decode:
    max_concurrency: 40
    token_budget_target: 102400
    batch_deadline_ms: 6
soft_limits:
  per_worker_inflight: 120
  kv_warmup_threshold: 3 # number of recent prefill hits to consider KV warm
kernel_affinity:
  decode: [family-B, family-A]
  prefill: [family-A]
```
lee: token_budget_target looks odd (prefill lower than decode). was that intentional?
maria: yes, we biased decode higher to keep streaming ramps smoother. prefill batches are more latency-sensitive so smaller budgets to form faster batches.
tim: suggestion: make token_budget_target adaptive by recent KV warmth metric instead of static. if kv_warmup_threshold false -> reduce decode concurrency and bump prefill priority.
olga: agree. also try migrating the kernel affinity change to a soft hint instead of hard forcing; fallback to family-A if KV eviction rate rises.
aj: add a backoff window where decode lanes drop to single-stream mode for 30s when eviction_rate > x.
maria: implemented local patch and re-ran short trial: eviction spike reduced by ~45%, p99 improved slightly but avg decode throughput dropped during backoff, as expected.
perf-bot: NOTE: regression detection flagged a small output-latency variance for long-context workloads after the affinity change; filing ticket: INF-6721.
lee: we should also add a per-worker KV usage gauge to the console so we can route by worker KV-pressure not just global.
maria: agree — I've sketched a dashboard and will open a PR with metrics + adaptive token-budget heuristics tomorrow. PR will include opt-in flags for the soft-affinity and decode backoff.
aj: for rollout plan, recommend canary on small bursty traffic first, monitor kv_evictions, p99, and token-efficiency. if any metric crosses threshold auto-fallback.
maria: plan: canary 3% traffic, 20m, alerts on kv_evictions_rate > 1.5x baseline or p99 regression > 10%. tagging @oncall in deploy notes.
olga: thanks — also capture kernel switch counts. those correlated strongly with eviction spikes.
tim: let's sync in tomorrow standup to lock the PR and thresholds. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
